question: Should exact requester-consumed descendant output count as durable descendant delivery proof, suppressing later descendant retry/finalization once matched by run ID, requester session, and run-start window?
rationale: Automation can verify the code path, but it cannot decide whether this delivery boundary is the intended product/runtime contract versus folding the case into the broader durable completion inbox work.

options.title: Require proof and boundary sign-off
options.body: Ask for redacted live cron/background or SQLite restore proof, then accept the patch only if the owner agrees requester consumption is sufficient delivery proof.

options.title: Accept the current boundary
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept that exact matched requester consumption suppresses descendant retry even if no separate descendant-visible delivery occurs.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this PR and handle the case in the broader durable completion inbox or spool design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Require proof and boundary sign-off
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted live cron/background or SQLite restore proof, then accept the patch only if the owner agrees requester consumption is sufficient delivery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits closest to the deterministic subagent announce and descendant gating behavior introduced in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/35080.
